newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's MES in 11,000 bpd Iraqi oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Russia's MES in 11,000 bpd Iraqi oil deal.

text.p: Russia's Organisation for Economic Cooperation, or MES, has signed a deal with Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organization for 11,000 barrels per day of Iraqi crude over six months, a top Russian oil executive said on Wednesday.

Yuri Agababov, deputy director of Zarubezhneft, which is coordinating Russian purchases of Iraqi oil, said MES, known in Russian as Mezhdunarodnoye Ekonomicheskoye Sotrudnichestvo, would export from Iraq's southern terminal Mina al-Bakr.
He did not know when lifting would begin.
Only three Russian companies -- LUKoil, Zarubezhneft and Nafta-Moskva, all of which have signed contracts whose amounts have not changed -- would lift from northern outlets, he said.

Agababov denied London oil market talk that one or more Russian companies, possibly LUKoil, had already sold Kirkuk crude into the international spot market in a transaction that would mark the first such sale of Iraqi oil since U.N. sanctions were slapped on Baghdad for its invasion of Kuwait in August 1990.
"No Russian companies have sold anything yet," he said.
